rows.title: Kernel evaluation of runs over a page-sized block: deep recursion / >11 GB
rows.request: **The kernel cannot evaluate a run that writes into a block of 4096 bytes.** `decide +kernel` on `do let p ← Zig.alloc .heap 4096 8; Zig.memset (α := BitVec 8) 1 p 16 none; Zig.store (α := BitVec 32) 4 p 7` from `{}` fails with "(kernel) deep recursion detected" (0.9 GB); the same with 16 bytes decides in 0.6 s. The L4 Controls hit it through the translated PageAllocator (every grant is a 4 KiB mapping): Open's `push` with a page-backed env (`create` -> `allocBytesAligned` memsets the 16 bytes, then `push` stores the fields) does not decide from a concrete start memory; raising `maxRecDepth` (4000 to 200000) makes `decide +kernel` and `unroll_solo` exceed 11 GB RSS (build-guard rss_limit). The page `alloc` alone decides (`PageAlloc.alloc_top`), and so do runs that only read the page or write it without a prior `memset`. Needed: one concrete admissible start memory in which `push` returns `.ok p`, evaluated (kernel-checked), so that the refutations of #74 are existential (natively right: `mmap` may fail, so no triple promises `.ok`). Likely cause: the kernel's representation of the 4096-byte `Array Byte` (list-backed; `writeBytes`/`extract`/`append` are linear recursions) under `memset` + `store`. Options: a bytes representation the kernel reduces with bounded depth (e.g. chunked or `ByteArray`-like with kernel-friendly ops), or a run lemma family that rewrites the memset/store effect on a symbolic block (`simp`/`fsym_norm` equations) instead of evaluating the array. Repro files: `~/.cache/air2lean/scratch/l4/T36.lean` (minimal), `T32.lean` (Open push with the page env from a precomputed memory, rss_limit), `T34.lean` (page alloc + memset + store).
